proof:
Source: parent proof step 3(i) (FTC along rays; Tonelli with the null x-sections σ⁻¹N_u).

1. Let D := {y : u is differentiable at y}. D is measurable (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt), and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D) = 0 (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, rewritten with ae_iff).

2. Let σ ≠ 0. Then {x : σx ∉ D} = (x ↦ σ•x)⁻¹(Dᶜ) has Lebesgue measure |σ^n|⁻¹·Lⁿ(Dᶜ) = 0 (MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_preimage_smul). So ∀ᵐ x, σx ∈ D.

3. The singleton {0} ⊂ ℝ is Lebesgue-null (Measure.ae_ne volume 0), so step 2 gives ∀ᵐ σ ∈ ℝ, ∀ᵐ x ∈ ℝⁿ, σx ∈ D. For σ = 0 the inner statement may fail, which is why only a.e. σ is used.

4. The set {(x, σ) : σ•x ∈ D} is measurable: it is the preimage of D under the continuous map (x, σ) ↦ σ•x. By MeasureTheory.Measure.ae_ae_comm (both measures σ-finite): for a.e. x ∈ ℝⁿ, for a.e. σ ∈ ℝ, σx ∈ D.

5. Fix such x and an arbitrary t ∈ ℝ. Apply Submission.dorag_ha_rb_line_ftc with p = 0, v = x, a = t, b = 1. Its hypothesis holds because 0 + σ•x = σ•x ∈ D for a.e. σ (rewrite with zero_add). It gives u(0 + 1•x) − u(0 + t•x) = ∫_t^1 Du(0 + σx)x dσ, which simplifies (zero_add, one_smul) to u(x) − u(tx) = ∫_t^1 Du(σx)x dσ. Since t was arbitrary, the claim holds for all t. ∎
